archetype.name: World Series Contender (complete roster)
archetype.definition: A team with the best margin in baseball, an A+ lineup, a true ace and a top bullpen, now one series from a title after going 7-1 through the National League bracket.

report.headline: The best team all year, and the October run matches the margin
report.take:
Milwaukee went 103-59 and ranked first on the site. The record is earned. Its Run Diff / G of 1.32 led the league, and the margin alone implies 102.5 wins, so the W vs Run Diff figure of 0.5 says almost none of this came from close-game luck. That is a change from 2024 and 2025, when the Brewers finished under their differential. This year the results finally caught up with the underlying team, and the team kept improving. The site ranked it 4th in 2024, 2nd in 2025 and 1st now.

The engine is a deep lineup playing in a pitcher's park. A Park factor of 96 suppresses offense, yet the Brewers scored 5.14 runs a game, 2nd in the league, with a team OPS 25 points above the league. Brice Turang (127 wRC+, 5.9 WAR, the top second baseman on the site), Jake Bauers (143 wRC+) and Jackson Chourio (130 wRC+) lead it, and enough supporting bats are above average to earn the hitters an A+. On the run-prevention side, Jacob Misiorowski is the story. He posted a 1.80 ERA backed by a 2.17 FIP and struck out 37.9% of the batters he faced. Behind him, a bullpen graded A, anchored by Trevor Megill (1.85 FIP, 30 saves) and Aaron Ashby, finishes games.

The numbers hide two softer spots. The first is the middle of the rotation. Dustin May, Shane Drohan and Kyle Harrison all ran ERAs in the 4s, so the B+ rotation grade is mostly Misiorowski. The second is the defense. The team's Fielding Runs fell to 8.2, 12th in the league, from 27.5 a year earlier, as weak gloves at third base and first base offset elite ones at short, second and in the outfield. The October numbers also flatter a little. The 7-1 run carries a postseason W vs Run Diff of 1.3, built on one-run wins like 3-2, 4-3 and 2-1.

Where it's heading is simple: the World Series, starting at home. The Brewers arrive in their best form of the year. They went 18-6 in September, won 8 of their last 10 regular-season games and swept the Dodgers 4-0 in the NLCS. This is the strongest team in the field by the regular-season numbers. It just needs the ace and the late innings to keep carrying the games the middle of the rotation starts.

strengths.title: A deep lineup beating its park
strengths.body: The Brewers scored the 2nd-most runs a game in the league despite a home park that plays below average for hitters. That says the offense is better than even its raw totals suggest. It is broad: Turang, Bauers, Chourio and Garrett Mitchell all posted wRC+ well above 100, which is why the group grades A+ instead of leaning on one star. Lineups this deep hold up in a short series because there's no single bat to pitch around.

strengths.title: Misiorowski is a genuine ace
strengths.body: A 1.80 ERA with a 2.17 FIP means his run prevention came from strikeouts and limited walks, not batted-ball luck, and 252 strikeouts in 174.2 innings made him the top starter on the site. His two postseason starts were shakier, with a 3.24 ERA and a 1.56 WHIP. Even so, his 1.90 postseason FIP says the stuff is still there.

strengths.title: A bullpen that closes the door
strengths.body: The relief corps graded A. Megill's 1.85 FIP says his 2.63 ERA was, if anything, unlucky. In October, Ashby has thrown 12.1 scoreless innings and Megill has 4 saves without allowing an earned run. That combination is why the Brewers have won so many one-run postseason games.

concerns.title: Starting depth behind the ace
concerns.body: May (4.70 ERA), Drohan (4.19) and Harrison (4.20) were average-or-worse run preventers. May's 3.63 FIP suggests some bad luck, but he has a 6.43 ERA in three October outings. In a seven-game series, the games Misiorowski doesn't start put a lot of weight on the bullpen, and that is the clearest path for an opponent to steal games.

concerns.title: October luck in close games
concerns.body: Three of the seven playoff wins were by one run, and the postseason W vs Run Diff of 1.3 ranks first among the playoff teams. The underlying margin is still strong, at a 1.63 Run Diff / G. But a run like this usually has a coin flip or two go the other way eventually. Some relievers also walk too many: DL Hall's 14.5% walk rate and 3.88 FIP sit far from his 1.91 ERA.

concerns.title: Defense slipped from its usual standard
concerns.body: Fielding Runs of 8.2 ranks only 12th in the league, a sharp drop from the 27.5 of 2025 and the 35.4 of 2023. The holes are at the corners: David Hamilton (-7.9 Def Runs at third) and Bauers (-5.5 at first). Elite fielders up the middle and in the outfield, Ortiz, Turang and Chourio, keep it from being a real weakness.

trend.note: After a 12-13 April, the Brewers posted a winning record every month and peaked late: 18-6 in September while scoring 6.08 runs a game. They then went 7-1 through the NLDS and NLCS, including a 4-0 sweep.

weekAhead.headline: World Series opens at home, then shifts on the road
weekAhead.body:
The week covers the first four games of the World Series: two at home on October 23 and 24, then two away on October 26 and 27. The sheet doesn't list the opponent, so this preview is about Milwaukee's own setup rather than the matchup. Opening at home in a park that suppresses hitting suits a staff that finished 2nd in ERA.

The pitching order is the real question. Misiorowski can likely take one of the four games and maybe set the tone in the opener. The rest falls to some mix of Logan Henderson, Robert Gasser and May. Gasser has been sharp in October (1.00 ERA in 9.0 innings) despite a 4.21 FIP that says he's been fortunate. With an off day in the middle of the week, the leverage relievers should be fresh enough to cover short starts.

keyMatchups.title: Misiorowski's command on the big stage
keyMatchups.body: His regular-season 0.80 WHIP turned into a 1.56 WHIP across two postseason starts, and his walk rate rose too. If he's back to his 37.9% strikeout form, Milwaukee is the clear favorite in whatever game he starts. If the command stays loose, the series gets much more even.

keyMatchups.title: Contreras hot, Chourio cold
keyMatchups.body: William Contreras has carried the October offense with a 212 wRC+ and 3 home runs. Chourio, a 130 wRC+ hitter all season, is at 48 in 38 plate appearances. A sample that small says little about his true talent. If Chourio's bat returns, the lineup gets much harder to navigate.

keyMatchups.title: Late innings belong to Ashby, Megill
keyMatchups.body: The two have combined for 6 postseason saves without allowing an earned run. That edge in late innings is what has turned close games into wins all month. How often the starters can hand them a lead decides how much it matters.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the non-Misiorowski starters can get through the order twice, so the Ashby-Megill tandem isn't stretched across four games.

restOfSeason.body:
By every season-long measure, this is the best team in the series: first in run differential per game, 2nd in runs scored, 4th in runs allowed, with grades of A+, B+ and A. It also comes in on its best form of the year. I'd make Milwaukee a moderate favorite, and I project it to finish with 9 to 11 playoff wins. That means a title or a series that runs deep before it ends.

What is sustainable: the lineup depth, Misiorowski's strikeouts and the late-inning tandem. What is likely to regress: the one-run postseason luck and Gasser's run prevention running well ahead of his FIP. Expect the World Series to be closer than the 4-0 sweep of the Dodgers. The margin for error is the gap between the ace and the rest of the rotation.
swingFactors: Middle-rotation starts from May and the others

confidence.note: The full-season numbers are robust, but the postseason samples are small and the opponent isn't on the sheet.
